title: GCD Calculator
description: Find the Greatest Common Divisor of two numbers with a full Euclidean algorithm step-by-step.

formula.summary: The Euclidean algorithm finds the GCD by repeatedly replacing the larger number with the remainder of dividing it by the smaller number, until the remainder reaches zero.
formula.expression: GCD(a, b) = GCD(b, a mod b), until b = 0

faqs.question: What is the GCD used for?
faqs.answer: The GCD is used to simplify fractions to lowest terms, solve certain algebra and number theory problems, and is a building block for the LCM calculation.

faqs.question: How fast is the Euclidean algorithm?
faqs.answer: Extremely fast - it's one of the oldest known algorithms and typically finishes in a small number of steps even for very large numbers, which is why it's still the standard method used today.

seoContent.heading: The Euclidean algorithm, step by step
seoContent.body: Named after the ancient Greek mathematician Euclid, this algorithm is one of the oldest continuously used algorithms in mathematics. It works by repeated division: divide the larger number by the smaller, keep the remainder, then repeat with the smaller number and that remainder, until the remainder is zero - the last nonzero remainder is the GCD.

seoContent.heading: Why the GCD matters for fractions
seoContent.body: Dividing both the numerator and denominator of a fraction by their GCD produces the same fraction in its simplest possible form. This is exactly what the Fraction Calculator and Decimal to Fraction Calculator do internally after computing a raw result.
